summary.en: Germanic tribes led by Arminius ambushed and destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus. The defeat ended Augustus's plans to push the frontier to the Elbe, leaving the Rhine as the lasting boundary of Roman power.
summary.zh: 阿米尼乌斯率领的日耳曼部落伏击并全歼瓦卢斯统率的三个罗马军团。此役使奥古斯都放弃将边界推进至易北河的计划，莱茵河由此成为罗马势力的长期边界。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest

note: Month (September 9 CE) is known but not the exact days; the battlefield is identified with the Kalkriese archaeological site (Wikidata coordinates), which most but not all scholars accept.

summary.en: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii, Herculaneum and neighbouring towns under ash and pyroclastic flows. Pliny the Younger's letters describe the disaster, in which his uncle Pliny the Elder died; the buried cities became key archaeological sites.
summary.zh: 维苏威火山喷发，火山灰和火山碎屑流掩埋了庞贝、赫库兰尼姆及周边城镇。小普林尼的书信记录了这场灾难，其舅父老普林尼在救援中遇难；被掩埋的城市后来成为重要的考古遗址。

sources.title: Pliny the Younger, Letters VI.16 and VI.20

note: Wikidata gives 24 October 79, supported by a charcoal inscription found at Pompeii in 2018; the manuscript tradition of Pliny's letter gives 24 August. The year is undisputed.

summary.en: On Emperor Hadrian's orders, Roman legions began building a stone and turf barrier about 118 km long across northern Britain, from the Tyne to the Solway Firth. It marked and controlled the empire's north-western frontier for most of the next three centuries.
summary.zh: 罗马军团奉哈德良皇帝之命，在不列颠北部自泰恩河至索尔威湾修筑长约118公里的石土城墙。此后近三百年间，它大体标志并管控着帝国的西北边疆。

sources.title: UNESCO: Frontiers of the Roman Empire

note: Construction began c. 122 and the main work was completed c. 128; both dates are approximate.

summary.en: Meeting in Milan, the emperors Constantine I and Licinius agreed to grant religious freedom throughout the empire and to restore confiscated property to Christians. The policy ended state persecution and opened the way for Christianity's rise to imperial favour.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世与李锡尼在米兰会晤，同意在帝国境内给予宗教自由，并归还被没收的基督徒财产。这一政策终结了官方迫害，为基督教获得帝国青睐铺平了道路。

note: The agreement was reached at Milan in February 313; the surviving text is a rescript issued by Licinius at Nicomedia in June 313.

summary.en: Constantine I formally dedicated his rebuilt city on the site of Byzantium as a new imperial residence, Constantinople. It became the capital of the eastern Roman, later Byzantine, empire for more than eleven centuries.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世在拜占庭旧址上重建城市，并正式将其奉献为新的帝国驻地——君士坦丁堡。此后一千一百余年，它一直是东罗马即拜占庭帝国的首都。

note: QID is the historical city of Constantinople, whose inception Wikidata gives as 330.

summary.en: Gothic forces, mainly Tervingi under Fritigern joined by Greuthungi cavalry, destroyed an eastern Roman army near Adrianople; Emperor Valens was killed. The disaster left the Goths settled inside the empire and is often seen as a turning point in the late Roman crisis.
summary.zh: 以弗里提格伦为首的哥特人（主要为特尔温吉部，并有格鲁森尼骑兵增援）在阿德里安堡附近歼灭东罗马军队，瓦伦斯皇帝阵亡。此役使哥特人得以定居帝国境内，常被视为罗马晚期危机的转折点。

note: Date is secure; the exact battlefield, some kilometres north of Adrianople (Edirne), is unknown—coordinates follow Wikidata's approximation.

name.en: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths

summary.en: Visigoths under Alaric I entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time in about 800 years that the city had fallen to a foreign enemy. The shock across the Roman world prompted Augustine to write The City of God.
summary.zh: 阿拉里克一世率领的西哥特人攻入罗马城并劫掠三日，这是近八百年来罗马首次落入外敌之手。此事震动整个罗马世界，促使奥古斯丁写下《上帝之城》。

sources.title: Orosius, Seven Books of History against the Pagans VII.39
Augustine, De civitate Dei, Book I

summary.en: A coalition of Romans under Flavius Aetius and Visigoths under Theodoric I fought Attila's Hunnic army in north-eastern Gaul. Theodoric fell, but Attila withdrew, ending his invasion of Gaul.
summary.zh: 罗马统帅埃提乌斯与西哥特国王狄奥多里克一世的联军，在高卢东北部迎战阿提拉的匈人大军。狄奥多里克阵亡，但阿提拉被迫撤退，其入侵高卢的行动就此终止。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains

note: The site is unknown—placed by sources between Châlons-en-Champagne and Troyes; the day (20 June, per Wikidata) is a modern reconstruction. Wikidata's English label is 'Battle of the Maureaco Fields'.

name.zh: 罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯被废黜

summary.en: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The date conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire, though its decline had been long and gradual.
summary.zh: 日耳曼将领奥多亚克在拉文纳废黜少年皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯，并将帝国徽章送往君士坦丁堡。这一年通常被视为西罗马帝国灭亡的标志，尽管其衰落是一个漫长渐进的过程。

sources.title: Peter Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire (2005)

summary.en: Clovis I, king of the Franks, was baptised a Catholic Christian by Bishop Remigius at Reims. Choosing Nicene Christianity rather than the Arianism of other Germanic kings won him the support of the Gallo-Roman church and population.
summary.zh: 法兰克国王克洛维一世在兰斯由主教雷米吉乌斯施洗，皈依天主教。他选择尼西亚派而非其他日耳曼诸王所信奉的阿里乌派，因而赢得高卢—罗马教会与民众的支持。

sources.title: Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks II.31

note: Gregory of Tours' chronology implies c. 496; modern historians place the baptism anywhere between 496 and 508. Wikidata has no date.

summary.en: Justinian I dedicated the rebuilt church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. Its vast dome made it the largest church in Christendom for nearly a thousand years.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼一世为君士坦丁堡重建的圣索菲亚大教堂举行献堂礼，该教堂由特拉勒斯的安提米乌斯和米利都的伊西多尔设计。其巨大的穹顶使之在近千年间都是基督教世界最大的教堂。

note: Wikidata's start date (23 February 532) is when rebuilding began; this record marks the dedication of 27 December 537.

summary.en: Bubonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, reached the Mediterranean through Egypt in 541 and struck Constantinople in 542, killing a large share of its population. Recurring waves until the mid-8th century weakened the Byzantine Empire and its neighbours.
summary.zh: 由鼠疫杆菌引起的腺鼠疫于541年经埃及传入地中海世界，542年侵袭君士坦丁堡，造成大量人口死亡。此后直至8世纪中叶的反复流行，削弱了拜占庭帝国及其邻邦。

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars II.22–23
Lester K. Little (ed.), Plague and the End of Antiquity: The Pandemic of 541–750 (2007)

note: Wikidata spans all waves (541–750); endYear here marks the first wave. Placed at Constantinople, the best-documented outbreak (542).

name.zh: 倭马亚王朝征服伊比利亚

summary.en: Berber and Arab forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa, defeated King Roderic at the Guadalete in 711 and within a few years overran most of the Visigothic kingdom. The conquest created al-Andalus, Muslim-ruled Iberia, which survived in part until 1492.
summary.zh: 塔里克·伊本·齐亚德率领柏柏尔人和阿拉伯人从北非渡海，711年在瓜达莱特河击败国王罗德里克，数年内攻占西哥特王国大部。这次征服建立了安达卢斯，穆斯林在伊比利亚的统治部分延续至1492年。

sources.title: Roger Collins, The Arab Conquest of Spain, 710–797 (1989)

note: Coordinates and date are those of the opening Battle of Guadalete (Wikidata Q504172); the span 711–726 follows Wikidata.

summary.en: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Umayyad army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, governor of al-Andalus, between Poitiers and Tours. The victory checked Muslim raids north of the Pyrenees and strengthened the Carolingian family's power.
summary.zh: 查理·马特率领的法兰克军队在普瓦捷与图尔之间击败安达卢斯总督阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·加菲基率领的倭马亚军队。此役遏制了穆斯林越过比利牛斯山向北的袭扰，并巩固了加洛林家族的权势。

sources.title: Continuations of the Chronicle of Fredegar

note: Traditionally 10 October 732 (Wikidata); a minority argue for 733. The site between Tours and Poitiers is uncertain; coordinates follow Wikidata (Moussais-la-Bataille).

summary.en: From the raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793 until the mid-11th century, Scandinavian seafarers raided, traded and settled from Ireland to the Volga. They founded the Kingdom of Jórvík, Normandy and the settlement of Iceland, and helped shape the early Rus' state.
summary.zh: 自793年袭击林迪斯法恩修道院起至11世纪中叶，斯堪的纳维亚航海者从爱尔兰到伏尔加河一带劫掠、贸易与定居。他们建立了约克维京王国和诺曼底，定居冰岛，并参与塑造了早期罗斯国家。

label.zh: 罗斯人袭击君士坦丁堡
留里克入主诺夫哥罗德（传说）

label.en: Harald Hardrada falls at Stamford Bridge
label.zh: 哈拉尔德·哈德拉达战死斯坦福桥

sources.title: Russian Primary Chronicle (Povest' vremennykh let), entry for 862

note: 793–1066 is a conventional span; Wikidata gives no dates. Several route dates (Novgorod 862, Iceland 874) are traditional.

summary.en: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day. The act revived a western imperial title, deepened the alliance between the papacy and the Franks, and strained relations with Byzantium.
summary.zh: 圣诞节当天，教宗利奥三世在圣伯多禄大殿为法兰克国王查理曼加冕为“罗马人的皇帝”。此举复兴了西方的帝号，加深了教廷与法兰克人的同盟，也使与拜占庭的关系趋于紧张。

sources.title: Royal Frankish Annals, entry for 801 (year reckoned from Christmas)

summary.en: The three surviving sons of Louis the Pious divided the Carolingian Empire: Charles the Bald took West Francia, Louis the German East Francia, and Lothair I a middle kingdom with the imperial title. The partition foreshadowed the later division between France and Germany.
summary.zh: 虔诚者路易的三个儿子瓜分加洛林帝国：秃头查理得西法兰克，日耳曼人路易得东法兰克，洛泰尔一世得中法兰克并保有皇帝称号。这次分割预示了日后法兰西与德意志的分野。

summary.en: Grand Prince Vladimir I of Kyiv accepted Byzantine Christianity, was baptised and had the people of Kyiv baptised in the Dnieper. The conversion tied the Rus' to the church and culture of Constantinople, shaping the later Orthodox identity of Ukraine, Belarus and Russia.
summary.zh: 基辅大公弗拉基米尔一世接受拜占庭基督教并受洗，随后令基辅民众在第聂伯河中受洗。这次皈依使罗斯与君士坦丁堡的教会和文化紧密相连，塑造了日后乌克兰、白俄罗斯和俄罗斯的东正教认同。

note: 988 is the Primary Chronicle's date; Vladimir's own baptism may have taken place at Chersonesos in Crimea, and some historians date it 987–989.

summary.en: Papal legates led by Cardinal Humbert laid a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of Hagia Sophia, and the patriarch replied in kind. The mutual excommunications came to symbolise the lasting split between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
summary.zh: 以枢机主教洪贝尔为首的教宗使节将绝罚君士坦丁堡宗主教米海尔·色路拉里乌斯的诏书置于圣索菲亚大教堂祭坛上，宗主教随即予以反绝罚。这次相互绝罚成为罗马天主教与东正教长期分裂的象征。

sources.title: Henry Chadwick, East and West: The Making of a Rift in the Church (2003)

note: The rupture was a long process; 1054 is its conventional symbolic date.

summary.en: Duke William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II near Hastings, opening the Norman conquest of England. William was crowned at Westminster on Christmas Day 1066, and a new French-speaking aristocracy transformed English government, language and architecture.
summary.zh: 诺曼底公爵威廉在黑斯廷斯附近击败并杀死英格兰国王哈罗德二世，开启诺曼征服。威廉于1066年圣诞节在威斯敏斯特加冕，说法语的新贵族阶层由此深刻改变了英格兰的政治、语言和建筑。

sources.title: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (MSS D and E), entry for 1066

summary.en: Answering Pope Urban II's call at Clermont in 1095, armies of western knights marched through Constantinople and Anatolia, took Antioch in 1098 and captured Jerusalem in July 1099. The crusade founded Latin states in the Levant.
summary.zh: 响应教宗乌尔班二世1095年在克莱蒙发出的号召，西欧骑士大军经君士坦丁堡、穿越安纳托利亚，于1098年攻占安条克，1099年7月攻陷耶路撒冷，并在黎凡特建立了一系列拉丁国家。

label.zh: 十字军集结莱茵兰（科隆）
大军经君士坦丁堡渡海

note: Wikidata's 'point in time' of 1090 appears erroneous; its start/end (1096–1099) are used. Event placed at Clermont, where the crusade was preached.

summary.en: Facing baronial rebellion, King John of England agreed at Runnymede to a charter limiting royal power and guaranteeing certain legal rights. Though annulled within months, its reissued versions became a foundation of English law and a symbol of constitutional government.
summary.zh: 面对贵族叛乱，英格兰国王约翰在兰尼米德同意颁布一份限制王权、保障若干法律权利的特许状。该文件数月后即被废止，但其后的重订版本成为英格兰法律的基石和宪政的象征。

sources.title: J. C. Holt, Magna Carta (3rd ed., 2015)

summary.en: A Mongol army under Batu Khan besieged and stormed Kyiv, the old capital of the Rus', destroying much of the city. Its fall completed the Mongol conquest of the Rus' principalities, which became tributaries of the Golden Horde.
summary.zh: 拔都率领的蒙古军队围攻并攻陷罗斯旧都基辅，城市大部被毁。基辅的陷落标志着蒙古对罗斯诸公国征服的完成，此后诸公国沦为金帐汗国的附庸。

note: Wikidata gives 28 Nov–6 Dec 1240; Rus' chronicles give differing days (some 19 Nov) for the fall.

summary.en: A series of wars between the Plantagenet kings of England and the Valois kings of France over the French crown and English lands in France. English victories such as Crécy and Agincourt were reversed after Joan of Arc helped relieve Orléans in 1429; by 1453 England held only Calais.
summary.zh: 英格兰金雀花王朝与法兰西瓦卢瓦王朝围绕法国王位及英格兰在法领地展开的一系列战争。英军虽有克雷西、阿金库尔等大捷，但1429年贞德助解奥尔良之围后局势逆转；至1453年英格兰仅保有加来。

sources.title: Jonathan Sumption, The Hundred Years War (5 vols., 1990–2023)

note: Placed at Orléans, the war's turning point (1429).

summary.en: Plague carried on Genoese ships from the Black Sea reached Sicily in October 1347 and swept across Europe within four years, killing perhaps a third to a half of the population. The catastrophe reshaped labour, religion and society across the continent.
summary.zh: 随热那亚船只从黑海传来的鼠疫于1347年10月抵达西西里，四年内席卷欧洲，可能造成三分之一至一半人口死亡。这场浩劫深刻改变了整个欧洲的劳动力、宗教与社会。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Decameron, Introduction to the First Day
Ole J. Benedictow, The Black Death 1346–1353: The Complete History (2004)

note: Wikidata dates the pandemic 1346–1352, starting in the Golden Horde; 1347 marks its arrival in Europe (Messina), and it reached Moscow in 1353, so endYear follows Benedictow.

summary.en: The allied armies of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas crushed the Teutonic Knights; Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen was killed. The defeat began the long decline of the Teutonic Order's state in Prussia.
summary.zh: 波兰王国与立陶宛大公国联军在瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃和维陶塔斯指挥下大败条顿骑士团，大团长乌尔里希·冯·容金根阵亡。此役开启了条顿骑士团国家在普鲁士的长期衰落。

sources.title: Jan Długosz, Annales seu cronicae incliti Regni Poloniae, Book XI

summary.en: Dante Alighieri completed the Commedia, an allegorical poem in three parts—Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso—written in the Tuscan vernacular during his exile. It became a founding work of Italian literature and of the literary Italian language.
summary.zh: 但丁在流亡期间完成了以托斯卡纳方言写成的寓言长诗《神曲》，分为《地狱篇》《炼狱篇》《天堂篇》三部。该作品成为意大利文学和意大利文学语言的奠基之作。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Trattatello in laude di Dante

note: Composed c. 1308–1321; Wikidata gives c. 1320. Paradiso was finished at Ravenna shortly before Dante's death in September 1321.

name.en: Founding of the University of Bologna

summary.en: Bologna's law school, traditionally dated to 1088, grew from teachers of Roman law into a university organised by student associations. Often regarded as the oldest university in continuous operation, it became a model for others across Europe.
summary.zh: 博洛尼亚的法学院按传统说法创立于1088年，由讲授罗马法的教师群体发展为由学生团体组织的大学。它通常被视为持续办学至今最古老的大学，并成为欧洲各地大学的典范。

sources.title: Hastings Rashdall, The Universities of Europe in the Middle Ages, vol. 1 (1895)

note: 1088 (Wikidata inception) is a traditional date fixed by a committee in the 1880s; teaching of law at Bologna is documented from the late 11th–12th century.

name.zh: 谷登堡《圣经》与活字印刷

summary.en: In Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg's workshop completed the 42-line Latin Bible, the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type. Printing spread to more than 200 European towns by 1500, transforming the circulation of knowledge.
summary.zh: 约翰内斯·谷登堡在美因茨的作坊完成了四十二行拉丁文《圣经》，这是欧洲首部以金属活字印刷的重要书籍。到1500年，印刷术已传播至欧洲两百多个城镇，彻底改变了知识的传播方式。

sources.title: Albert Kapr, Johann Gutenberg: The Man and His Invention (1996)

note: The Bible has no colophon; it is dated c. 1454–55 from a letter of Enea Silvio Piccolomini (March 1455) and a rubricator's note of 1456. Wikidata has no date.

summary.en: After a siege of about seven weeks, the Ottoman army of Sultan Mehmed II stormed Constantinople; the last emperor, Constantine XI Palaiologos, died in the fighting. The conquest ended the Byzantine Empire and made the city the Ottoman capital.
summary.zh: 经过约七周的围攻，苏丹穆罕默德二世的奥斯曼军队攻破君士坦丁堡，末代皇帝君士坦丁十一世·巴列奥略战死。此役终结了拜占庭帝国，该城随后成为奥斯曼帝国的首都。

sources.title: Kritoboulos of Imbros, History of Mehmed the Conqueror
Steven Runciman, The Fall of Constantinople 1453 (1965)

summary.en: After a ten-year war (1482–1492), Emir Muhammad XII surrendered Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, to Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile. The surrender completed the Christian Reconquista.
summary.zh: 经过十年战争（1482—1492年），埃米尔穆罕默德十二世将伊比利亚最后的穆斯林政权格拉纳达交给阿拉贡的斐迪南二世与卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝拉一世，基督教的“收复失地运动”至此完成。

sources.title: L. P. Harvey, Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500 (1990)

note: QID is the Granada War; Wikidata's start date for it (1492) conflicts with the standard 1482 start, so only the surrender date is used here.

summary.en: Sailing for the Crown of Castile, Christopher Columbus left Palos with three ships, crossed the Atlantic via the Canary Islands and reached the Bahamas on 12 October 1492. His return in 1493 launched sustained European contact with, and colonisation of, the Americas.
summary.zh: 哥伦布受卡斯蒂利亚王室资助，率三艘船从帕洛斯出发，经加那利群岛横渡大西洋，于1492年10月12日抵达巴哈马。1493年他返航后，欧洲开始与美洲持续接触并殖民美洲。

label.zh: 离开加那利群岛戈梅拉岛
登陆瓜纳哈尼（圣萨尔瓦多岛）

label.en: Santa María wrecked; La Navidad founded
label.zh: 圣玛丽亚号触礁，建立纳维达德

sources.title: Christopher Columbus, Diario of the First Voyage (abstract by Bartolomé de las Casas)
Samuel Eliot Morison, Admiral of the Ocean Sea (1942)

note: The Wikidata item covers all four voyages (1492–1504); this record is the first.

name.zh: 路德发表《九十五条论纲》

summary.en: Martin Luther, a theology professor at Wittenberg, circulated 95 theses disputing the sale of indulgences and sent them to Archbishop Albert of Mainz. Rapidly printed and spread, they sparked the Protestant Reformation that divided Western Christianity.
summary.zh: 维滕贝格大学神学教授马丁·路德提出《九十五条论纲》，抨击出售赎罪券，并寄呈美因茨大主教阿尔布雷希特。论纲经印刷迅速传播，引发了导致西方基督教分裂的宗教改革。

sources.title: Martin Luther, Disputatio pro declaratione virtutis indulgentiarum (1517)

note: Luther's covering letter to Archbishop Albert is dated 31 October 1517; whether he also nailed the theses to the Castle Church door is debated.

name.zh: 哥白尼出版《天体运行论》

summary.en: Nicolaus Copernicus's De revolutionibus orbium coelestium was printed in Nuremberg shortly before his death. Placing the Sun near the centre of the universe with Earth orbiting it, the book laid the groundwork for the Scientific Revolution.
summary.zh: 哥白尼的《天体运行论》在纽伦堡付印，出版于他去世前不久。该书提出太阳位于宇宙中心附近、地球绕其运行，为科学革命奠定了基础。

sources.title: Owen Gingerich, The Book Nobody Read (2004)

summary.en: The parliament meeting at Lublin turned the personal union of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania into a single Commonwealth with a jointly elected monarch and common Sejm. The new state was one of Europe's largest until its partitions in the late 18th century.
summary.zh: 在卢布林召开的议会将波兰王国与立陶宛大公国的君合国转变为统一的联邦，两国共同选举君主、设立共同议会。这一新国家在18世纪末被瓜分之前，一直是欧洲面积最大的国家之一。

sources.title: Norman Davies, God's Playground: A History of Poland, vol. 1 (1981)

summary.en: Philip II of Spain sent a fleet of about 130 ships to escort an invasion army from Flanders to England. Harried in the Channel, scattered by fireships off Calais and beaten at Gravelines, the Armada fled round Scotland and Ireland, losing many ships to storms.
summary.zh: 西班牙国王腓力二世派出约130艘战舰，意图护送驻佛兰德的军队入侵英格兰。无敌舰队在英吉利海峡遭英舰袭扰，在加来外海被火船冲散，又在格拉沃利讷战败，被迫绕道苏格兰和爱尔兰返航，途中因风暴损失惨重。

sources.title: Garrett Mattingly, The Defeat of the Spanish Armada (1959)
Colin Martin and Geoffrey Parker, The Spanish Armada (1988)

note: Event coordinates follow Wikidata (off Plymouth, the first engagement). English contemporaries used Old Style dates, ten days behind the Spanish (New Style) ones.

summary.en: Beginning with the Defenestration of Prague, a revolt of Bohemian Protestants against Habsburg rule grew into a European war involving the Holy Roman Empire, Sweden, Denmark, France and Spain. The fighting devastated Germany, where perhaps a fifth or more of the population died.
summary.zh: 以布拉格掷出窗外事件为开端，波希米亚新教徒反抗哈布斯堡统治的起义演变为一场席卷欧洲的大战，神圣罗马帝国、瑞典、丹麦、法国和西班牙相继卷入。战火重创德意志地区，可能有五分之一以上的人口丧生。

sources.title: Peter H. Wilson, Europe's Tragedy: A History of the Thirty Years War (2009)

note: Placed at Prague Castle, site of the Defenestration of 23 May 1618.

summary.en: The Roman Inquisition found Galileo Galilei 'vehemently suspect of heresy' for defending Copernican heliocentrism in his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems. He was forced to recant and spent his remaining years under house arrest near Florence.
summary.zh: 罗马宗教裁判所认定伽利略因在《关于两大世界体系的对话》中为哥白尼日心说辩护而“有强烈异端嫌疑”。他被迫公开放弃其观点，余生在佛罗伦萨附近遭软禁。

sources.title: Maurice A. Finocchiaro (ed.), The Galileo Affair: A Documentary History (1989)

note: The Wikidata item covers the whole Galileo affair (1610–1633); this record marks the sentence and abjuration at Santa Maria sopra Minerva on 22 June 1633.

summary.en: Treaties signed at Osnabrück and Münster ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic. They recognised Dutch and Swiss independence, extended toleration to Calvinists and strengthened the sovereignty of the German princes.
summary.zh: 在奥斯纳布吕克与明斯特签订的一系列条约，结束了神圣罗马帝国境内的三十年战争以及西班牙与荷兰共和国之间的八十年战争。和约承认荷兰与瑞士独立，将宗教宽容扩展至加尔文派，并增强了德意志诸侯的主权。

note: The Spanish–Dutch Peace of Münster was signed on 30 January 1648; the imperial treaties on 24 October 1648 (Wikidata date).

summary.en: A relief army of imperial, German and Polish–Lithuanian troops under King John III Sobieski routed the Ottoman forces of Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha besieging Vienna. The victory began a long Habsburg counter-offensive that recovered Hungary by 1699.
summary.zh: 由神圣罗马帝国、德意志诸邦和波兰—立陶宛军队组成、波兰国王扬三世·索别斯基统率的援军，击溃了围攻维也纳的大维齐尔卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏的奥斯曼军队。此役开启了哈布斯堡王朝的长期反攻，至1699年收复匈牙利。

sources.title: John Stoye, The Siege of Vienna (1964)

name.zh: 牛顿《自然哲学的数学原理》出版

summary.en: Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, issued in London under the Royal Society's imprimatur at Edmond Halley's expense, set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation. It unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics and became a foundation of modern physics.
summary.zh: 牛顿的《自然哲学的数学原理》经皇家学会批准在伦敦出版，费用由埃德蒙·哈雷承担。书中提出运动定律和万有引力定律，统一了地面力学与天体力学，成为近代物理学的基石。

sources.title: Richard S. Westfall, Never at Rest: A Biography of Isaac Newton (1980)

note: Wikidata's inception (1680) reflects when Newton began the work; publication was on 5 July 1687.

summary.en: Peter the Great's Russian army decisively defeated Charles XII of Sweden near Poltava in the Great Northern War. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and established Russia as the dominant state of north-eastern Europe.
summary.zh: 大北方战争中，彼得大帝的俄军在波尔塔瓦附近决定性地击败瑞典国王卡尔十二世。此役终结了瑞典的强国时代，确立了俄国在东北欧的主导地位。

sources.title: Peter Englund, The Battle That Shook Europe: Poltava and the Birth of the Russian Empire (2003)

note: Wikidata gives 27 June 1709, the Julian (Old Style) date used in Russia; 8 July is the Gregorian date (28 June in the Swedish calendar).

summary.en: On All Saints' Day a great earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The disaster prompted Pombal's planned rebuilding of the city and fuelled Enlightenment debate about providence, notably in Voltaire's writings.
summary.zh: 万圣节当天，一场大地震及随后的海啸和大火摧毁了里斯本大部分城区，造成数万人死亡。灾后庞巴尔侯爵主持规划重建，这场灾难也引发了以伏尔泰为代表的启蒙思想家关于天意的辩论。

sources.title: Voltaire, Poème sur le désastre de Lisbonne (1756)

note: Wikidata's coordinates (36.0, −11.0) are the estimated offshore epicentre; this record is placed at Lisbon, the city destroyed.

summary.en: Fiscal crisis and Enlightenment ideas led the Estates-General of 1789 to transform itself into a National Assembly; the storming of the Bastille on 14 July became the Revolution's symbol. It abolished feudal privilege and the monarchy, proclaimed the Rights of Man, and ended with Napoleon Bonaparte's coup in 1799.
summary.zh: 财政危机与启蒙思想促使1789年的三级会议转变为国民议会，7月14日攻占巴士底狱成为革命的象征。大革命废除了封建特权和君主制，发表《人权宣言》，最终以1799年拿破仑·波拿巴发动政变告终。

sources.title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (1789)
William Doyle, The Oxford History of the French Revolution (1989)

note: Coordinates are those of the Bastille (Wikidata Q6539).

summary.en: Napoleon crossed the Niemen with some 450,000 men of the Grande Armée, won a costly victory at Borodino and entered a burning Moscow in September. Without a Russian surrender, the retreat through winter, hunger and Cossack attacks destroyed most of his army.
summary.zh: 拿破仑率领约45万人的大军渡过涅曼河，在博罗季诺付出惨重代价取胜，9月进入陷于大火的莫斯科。俄国拒不求和，大军在严寒、饥饿与哥萨克袭扰中撤退，几乎全军覆没。

label.zh: 小雅罗斯拉韦茨战役，开始撤退

sources.title: Adam Zamoyski, 1812: Napoleon's Fatal March on Moscow (2004)

note: Estimates of the invading force range from about 450,000 to over 600,000 including reinforcements. Event placed at Borodino.

summary.en: Diplomats of the great powers, led by Metternich, Castlereagh, Alexander I and Talleyrand, redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon's defeat. The settlement, signed in June 1815, sought a balance of power and kept general peace among the great powers for decades.
summary.zh: 以梅特涅、卡斯尔雷、亚历山大一世和塔列朗为代表的列强外交官，在拿破仑战败后重新划定欧洲版图。1815年6月签署的最后议定书追求均势，使列强之间维持了数十年的大体和平。

sources.title: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815)

note: Held September 1814 – June 1815 (Wikidata start/end); Wikidata point in time 1815 refers to the Final Act of 9 June 1815.

summary.en: An Anglo-allied army under the Duke of Wellington and a Prussian army under Blücher defeated Napoleon south of Brussels. The defeat ended his Hundred Days' return to power; he abdicated again and was exiled to Saint Helena.
summary.zh: 威灵顿公爵统率的英国及其盟军与布吕歇尔统率的普鲁士军队在布鲁塞尔以南击败拿破仑。此役终结了他重掌政权的“百日王朝”，拿破仑再度退位并被流放至圣赫勒拿岛。

sources.title: Andrew Roberts, Waterloo: Napoleon's Last Gamble (2005)

summary.en: A wave of liberal and national uprisings spread from Palermo and Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan. Most were suppressed by 1849, but serfdom was abolished in the Austrian lands and the revolutions shaped later national movements.
summary.zh: 一股自由主义和民族主义起义浪潮从巴勒莫和巴黎蔓延至维也纳、柏林、布达佩斯和米兰。多数起义到1849年遭到镇压，但奥地利境内废除了农奴制，这场革命也深刻影响了此后的民族运动。

note: The wave began in Palermo on 12 January 1848 (Wikidata start date); placed at Paris, where the February Revolution triggered the wider uprisings.

name.en: Darwin's On the Origin of Species

summary.en: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, published in London by John Murray, argued that species evolve over generations through natural selection. The book transformed biology and provoked wide religious and philosophical debate.
summary.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文的《物种起源》由伦敦约翰·默里出版社出版，提出物种通过自然选择代代演化。此书彻底改变了生物学，并引发广泛的宗教与哲学争论。

sources.title: The Complete Work of Charles Darwin Online (ed. John van Wyhe)
Janet Browne, Charles Darwin: The Power of Place (2002)
Britannica: On the Origin of Species

summary.en: Led by Piedmont-Sardinia's prime minister Cavour and the volunteer campaigns of Giuseppe Garibaldi, most Italian states were united and the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in Turin in 1861 under Victor Emmanuel II. Venetia joined in 1866, and Rome, taken in 1870, became the capital in 1871.
summary.zh: 在撒丁王国首相加富尔的主导和朱塞佩·加里波第志愿军的征战下，意大利大部分邦国得以统一，1861年在都灵宣告成立以维克托·伊曼纽尔二世为国王的意大利王国。威尼托于1866年并入，1870年攻占的罗马于1871年成为首都。

sources.title: Lucy Riall, Risorgimento: The History of Italy from Napoleon to Nation State (2009)

note: Wikidata dates the Risorgimento 1815–1871; this record runs from the proclamation of the kingdom in Turin (17 March 1861) to Rome becoming capital (1871).

summary.en: After Prussian victories over Denmark, Austria and France engineered by Otto von Bismarck, King Wilhelm I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. The new German Empire became continental Europe's leading industrial and military power.
summary.zh: 在俾斯麦主导下，普鲁士先后战胜丹麦、奥地利和法国，随后普鲁士国王威廉一世在凡尔赛宫镜厅被宣布为德意志皇帝。新成立的德意志帝国成为欧洲大陆首屈一指的工业与军事强国。

sources.title: Christopher Clark, Iron Kingdom: The Rise and Downfall of Prussia, 1600–1947 (2006)

note: QID is the unification process (1866–1871), whose point in time in Wikidata is the proclamation of 18 January 1871.

summary.en: Triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, war between the Central Powers and the Allies brought trench deadlock in the west and vast campaigns in the east. About 9–10 million soldiers died, and the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires collapsed.
summary.zh: 奥匈帝国皇储弗朗茨·斐迪南大公在萨拉热窝遇刺，引发同盟国与协约国之间的大战，西线陷入堑壕僵持，东线则展开大规模运动战。约九百万至一千万军人阵亡，德意志、奥匈、俄罗斯和奥斯曼四大帝国相继崩溃。

sources.title: Hew Strachan, The First World War (2003)

note: Placed at Verdun on the Western Front (Wikidata has no coordinates). Wikidata point in time (11 Nov 1918) is the Armistice; start and end dates match.

summary.en: The Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin overthrew Russia's Provisional Government in Petrograd, seizing the Winter Palace. Their seizure of power led to civil war and to the founding of the Soviet Union in 1922.
summary.zh: 列宁领导的布尔什维克在彼得格勒推翻俄国临时政府，攻占冬宫。这次夺权引发了内战，并导致1922年苏联的建立。

sources.title: John Reed, Ten Days That Shook the World (1919)
Orlando Figes, A People's Tragedy: The Russian Revolution 1891–1924 (1996)

note: Wikidata gives 25 October 1917, the Julian date then used in Russia; 7 November is the Gregorian equivalent. Coordinates: Winter Palace.

summary.en: Signed in the Hall of Mirrors five years to the day after the Sarajevo assassination, the treaty ended the war between Germany and the Allies. Germany lost territory and colonies and accepted limits on its armed forces and liability for reparations; the treaty also created the League of Nations.
summary.zh: 和约在萨拉热窝事件整整五年后于凡尔赛宫镜厅签署，结束了德国与协约国之间的战争。德国丧失领土和殖民地，接受军备限制并承担赔款责任；和约还创建了国际联盟。

sources.title: Margaret MacMillan, Peacemakers: The Paris Conference of 1919 and Its Attempt to End War (2001)

note: Signed 28 June 1919; Wikidata's start date (10 January 1920) is its entry into force.

name.zh: 第二次世界大战（欧洲战场）

summary.en: Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 began a war that by 1941 pitted the Axis against Britain, the Soviet Union and the United States. In Europe it ended with Germany's unconditional surrender in May 1945, after tens of millions of deaths, including some six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust.
summary.zh: 1939年9月1日德国入侵波兰，战争爆发；至1941年，轴心国已与英国、苏联和美国全面交战。欧洲战事以1945年5月德国无条件投降告终，战争造成数千万人死亡，其中包括在大屠杀中遇害的约六百万犹太人。

label.zh: 韦斯特普拉特：入侵波兰

label.en: Battle of Britain and the Blitz
label.zh: 不列颠之战与伦敦大轰炸

sources.title: Gerhard L. Weinberg, A World at Arms: A Global History of World War II (1994)

note: Wikidata's end date (2 September 1945) is the global end with Japan's surrender; the war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945.

summary.en: Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 in Operation Barbarossa, opening the largest land war in history. After defeats at Moscow, Stalingrad and Kursk, the Red Army drove west and took Berlin in May 1945; Soviet deaths reached roughly 27 million.
summary.zh: 1941年6月22日，德国及其盟国发动“巴巴罗萨行动”入侵苏联，开启了史上规模最大的陆地战争。德军在莫斯科、斯大林格勒和库尔斯克相继失利后，红军一路西进，于1945年5月攻克柏林；苏联死亡人数约达2700万。

label.zh: 巴格拉季昂行动（明斯克）
维斯瓦河—奥得河攻势（华沙）

sources.title: David M. Glantz and Jonathan M. House, When Titans Clashed: How the Red Army Stopped Hitler (1995)

note: Soviet death estimates vary (c. 24–27 million, military and civilian).

summary.en: German and Axis forces fought to take Stalingrad on the Volga in months of street fighting. A Soviet counter-offensive in November 1942 encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943—a turning point of the war in Europe.
summary.zh: 德国及轴心国军队为夺取伏尔加河畔的斯大林格勒，展开了长达数月的巷战。1942年11月苏军发动反攻，包围德军第六集团军，后者于1943年2月投降，此役成为欧洲战场的转折点。

summary.en: On D-Day, American, British, Canadian and other Allied forces landed on five beaches in Normandy in the largest seaborne invasion in history. The landings opened a western front that, together with the Soviet advance in the east, led to Germany's defeat.
summary.zh: D日当天，美、英、加等盟军在诺曼底五处海滩登陆，这是史上规模最大的海上登陆作战。登陆开辟了西线战场，与东线苏军的推进一道导致德国战败。

sources.title: Antony Beevor, D-Day: The Battle for Normandy (2009)

summary.en: Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and West Germany signed treaties in Rome creating the European Economic Community and Euratom. The EEC's common market became the core of what later developed into the European Union.
summary.zh: 比利时、法国、意大利、卢森堡、荷兰和联邦德国在罗马签署条约，建立欧洲经济共同体和欧洲原子能共同体。欧共体的共同市场成为日后欧洲联盟的核心。

sources.title: EUR-Lex: Treaty establishing the European Economic Community (1957)

note: Signed on the Capitoline Hill (Palazzo dei Conservatori).

summary.en: A flawed safety test caused reactor No. 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine to explode, spreading radioactive contamination across much of Europe. Some 116,000 people were evacuated in 1986, and a 30-km exclusion zone remains.
summary.zh: 一次存在缺陷的安全测试导致苏联乌克兰切尔诺贝利核电站4号反应堆爆炸，放射性污染扩散至欧洲大部分地区。1986年约11.6万人被疏散，30公里隔离区至今仍在。

sources.title: International Atomic Energy Agency, INSAG-7: The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1 (1992)

summary.en: Amid mass protests and an exodus of East Germans, the GDR's announcement of eased travel rules led crowds to force open the Berlin Wall's checkpoints on the night of 9 November. The event symbolised the end of the Cold War division of Europe and led to German reunification in October 1990.
summary.zh: 在大规模抗议和东德民众出逃潮中，民主德国宣布放宽出行限制，11月9日夜民众涌向柏林墙并迫使检查站开放。这一事件象征着冷战时期欧洲分裂的终结，并促成1990年10月的两德统一。

sources.title: Mary Elise Sarotte, The Collapse: The Accidental Opening of the Berlin Wall (2014)

summary.en: After the failed August coup and independence declarations by the republics, the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agreed in December to replace the USSR with the Commonwealth of Independent States. Gorbachev resigned on 25 December and the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist the next day.
summary.zh: 八月政变失败、各加盟共和国纷纷宣布独立后，俄罗斯、乌克兰和白俄罗斯领导人于12月商定以独立国家联合体取代苏联。戈尔巴乔夫于12月25日辞职，苏联于次日正式解体。

sources.title: Serhii Plokhy, The Last Empire: The Final Days of the Soviet Union (2014)
Britannica: Collapse of the Soviet Union

note: Wikidata's coordinates (65, 90) are a centroid of the USSR; this record is placed at the Moscow Kremlin.
